rationale: Thin Preterit cell (1 existing): an indefinite l-marked cougher contrasts with the named l-marked participant of the inherited quotation.

data.turoyo: Qayəm šʕile, maḥəsse la greʕe, maḥəsla l barṯe du paša.
data.translation: Darauf hustete er, die Diener erwachten, und auch die Tochter des Statthalters.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: a short independently understandable event-and-consequence context. The old prs 117/37 citation is retained pending reference concordance rather than silently corrected.

data.turoyo: ʕAbər yatu mbalašle šoʕəl w mʕaṭəš w mʕaraṭle.
data.translation: Er kam herein und setzte sich und fing an zu husten und zu niesen und zu furzen.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: the supplied 75/38 text has bare šoʕəl after mbalašle, unlike the already printed košoʕəl prediction. Its reference was present, but this onset context and actual form were not quoted.

summary: All five occurrences remain stem I sense 1 husten. Coughing as a signal or as an event that wakes others does not create a separate sense.

The bodily event has no patient: Preterit uses L-series marking and can add an l-marked full participant NP (lu kurəko) or indefinite l ḥa. This coding is compatible with intransitive cough semantics; it does not make the participant an object.
Infectum occurs both with ko- in a predicted action and bare as a complement of mbalašle. The German wording “fing an zu husten” does not turn the form into an Infinitiv.
Coordination with mʕaṭəš “sneeze” belongs to the narrative description, not an independently established fixed Idiomatic phrases item.
Confirm the old page/line-to-text/verse concordance for prs 43/21,22 and prs 117/37, especially whether the latter points to PrS 42/33. Existing references and wording have not been emended.
